title: Large language models create an uneven informational layer over cities

bias_targets.methodology: Generating synthetic user profiles with varying household income levels and analyzing the price level, popularity, and visitor income segregation of recommended venues, as well as running regressions on neighborhood-level socioeconomic covariates (e.g., median income, bachelor ratio) against hallucination and algorithmic invisibility rates.
Varying the age dimension across 8 brackets in synthetic user profiles and comparing the spatial proximity, popularity, price level, and segregation of the venues surfaced by the LLMs.
Altering the sex attribute (male, female) in synthetic user prompts to measure differences in the visitation rates, prices, and visitor demographics of the recommended establishments.

Modifying the residential status of the user profile (e.g., local resident vs. tourist) and evaluating how recommendations shift, alongside mapping the uneven distribution of algorithmic invisibility (NAIR) and hallucination rates across 304 distinct urban neighborhoods.
